sources.outlet: Jim Omartian, UNC Kenan-Flagler working paper 'Do Banks Aid and Abet Asset Concealment: Evidence from the Panama Papers' (hosted by UCLA Anderson)
sources.quote: Once the EUSD comes into force, the incorporation activity indeed subsides relative to the pre-July 1 rush, but remains higher than the early period.
sources.searcher_note: Uses Mossack Fonseca (Panama Papers) incorporations 2002-2007; finds a pre-July 2005 rush from EUSD-country investors (+20 pp probability of any incorporation, ~73% more incorporations) and that Swiss-intermediary entities are the proxy for Swiss banks. Same finding, same firm; no 2,331-to-4,701 count. First draft dated 2016-09-02; current draft 2017-10-23. Other sentences in the PDF carry 'ff' ligatures, so a ligature-free sentence was chosen.

sources.outlet: Sven Giegold MEP, Greens/EFA, for European Parliament PANA committee hearing of Jean-Claude Juncker
sources.quote: Figure 3 shows that the creation of offshore companies via Mossack-Fonseca by Luxembourg reached an all-time high of almost 1300 in 2005, the year when the EUSTD entered into force.
sources.searcher_note: Names Mossack Fonseca and ties its 2005 formation peak to the EU Savings Tax Directive, for Luxembourg-linked formations (the lead says Swiss/Luxembourg/Monaco middlemen carry 69% of the jump). Annual count, not Apr-Jun quarter. PDF text extraction renders 'all-time' as 'all -time'.

sources.outlet: Journal of Public Policy (Paul and Matthew Caruana-Galizia)
sources.quote: We show that the growth of EU-owned entities declined immediately after the Directive’s implementation, whereas that of non-EU-owned entities remained stable.
sources.searcher_note: Uses the 2013 Offshore Leaks data from two other firms (not Mossack Fonseca); EUSD response seen as a post-July 2005 decline in EU-owned entities and substitution to non-cooperative jurisdictions. Pattern source; no pre-deadline doubling reported in the abstract.

notes: Two sources name Mossack Fonseca and tie a 2005 formation spike to the EU Savings Directive: Omartian's Panama Papers working paper (pre-July 1, 2005 rush) and a 2017 Greens/EFA PANA-committee paper (Luxembourg-sourced Mossack Fonseca formations peaked near 1,300 in 2005). A search snippet attributed 'affected investors roughly doubled offshore entity incorporations' to the ResearchGate/SSRN abstract of Omartian's 'Tax Information Exchange and Offshore Entities: Evidence from the Panama Papers', but both pages returned 403/bot checks, so it is not recorded as evidence. No source found with the Bahamas registry (1,656 to 3,108) or Nevis registry (684 to 1,353) figures, or the Asia-facing providers comparison. ICIJ's 2016 Mossack Fonseca gatekeeper story mentions the 2005 BVI bearer-share crackdown, not the savings directive. No disagreeing source found; no coverage dated after 2026-06-30 found.
